title: Chicken With Vinegar
description:
Chicken with vinegar, a “three-star peasant dish,” is one of the great poultry dishes from the area around Lyons, France, where the chickens are considered by many to be the best in the world. The variations are numerous, but the piercing flavor of vinegar is so dominant that it matters little whether you use shallots or garlic, thyme or tarragon. You could also add some mushrooms to the sauté.
One technical note: Most wine vinegar sold in the United States has an acidity level of 7 percent; many French vinegars are just 5 percent acidity. So it's best to cut strong vinegar with some wine or water, as noted here. Paul Bocuse's famous version: In Step 1, brown chicken in 7 tablespoons butter. In Step 3, add 3 tablespoons butter to reduced sauce.
This is great with a plain cheese risotto, or mashed potatoes, or some noodles, and a nice green salad.
ingredients: 3-pound chicken, cut up for sautéing, or 4-6 thighs
Salt and freshly ground black pepper
¼ cup minced shallots or onion
1-2 ripe tomatoes, peeled, cored, seeded, and cut into little pieces (or a can of diced tomatoes, or a good shot of tomato paste)
½ cup dry white wine or water
directions: Heat oil/butter until sizzling Add chicken pieces, and cook until pieces are lightly browned, about 8 minutes, flipping once after 5 minutes. Remove from pan for a few minutes and sprinkle liberally with salt and pepper.
Add the shallots to the pan a cook gently for 2 minutes, then garlic for another ½ minute.
Add the cup of vinegar/wine/water and tomatoes, and bring mixture to a gentle boil for minute or two, or until the powerful acrid smell has subsided somewhat.
Nestle the chicken back into the vinegar/tomato mixture, cover the pan, and cook in the oven for around 15 minutes.
Transfer the chicken to the serving dish.
If necessary, skim and discard any excess fat from surface of mixture in skillet. Also, if necessary or desired, continue to cook over low heat, until reduced a bit, 3 to 4 minutes.
Add salt to taste. Whisk in 1-2 tablespoons butter, maybe some crème fraiche, until incorporated.
Pour sauce over chicken, maybe decorate with some chopped parsley, and serve immediately.
